cosy-slide.title: Lesson Overview

cosy-image.alt: Cozy setting with tea and blanket

cosy-slide.p: How do you relax after a difficult week? In a noisy bar with friends or at home, under a cosy blanket, with a book? What do you know about relaxation techniques like hygge, coorie, and kalsarikännit?

cosy-blockquote.p: Today for 50 minutes, we're going to talk about relaxation and introduce you to the most effective relaxation techniques. It won't be about extreme forms of relaxation, but rather about being comfortable with yourself, and peace and concentration. Among other things, it helps effective language learning. Have a nice lesson!

ul.li: to discuss relaxation techniques typical of different countries;
to enlarge vocabulary on the topic of rest;
to learn new ways of talking about present habits.

cosy-vocabulary-item.definition: giving a feeling of comfort and warmth
to relax after a period of work
to sit or lie in a comfortable position with legs pulled up
to be likely to act or behave in a particular way
likely or liable to suffer from, do, or experience something
to continue doing something continuously or repeatedly

cosy-grammar-material.title: Structures to describe habits (tend to, be prone to, keep doing, as a rule)

cosy-slide.title: Ways to Relieve Stress

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to lead into the topic and generate interest.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Look at the comments and discuss them with your teacher

cosy-blockquote.p: I usually meet my friends in a bar somewhere to have a beer. We have a talk about the usual stuff. When you share some problems, they don't seem so serious anymore.
Here in France, people value beauty a lot. We call it "art of life"! When I dress up on Friday evening and sip a glass of good wine in a cafe, I feel rested and pleased.
Stress? Seriously? Here in Spain, we don't have stress ... because we take siestas!
